alerts.reason: June revenue grew 8.57% year over year, and service orders rose 12%, supporting a September forecast above -5%. Equipment orders fell 6% and activity was already lower in OFS and OFE. I expect weaker equipment orders to weigh on later deliveries and push December-quarter consolidated revenue down at least 5% year over year (A, B).

Astec's order backlog rose 139.7% year over year, supporting a September sales forecast above -5%. Yet June sales grew only 4.8% and fell sequentially from $284.4 million to $278.0 million. With labor shortages already affecting operations, I expect delayed shipments to push December-quarter sales down at least 5% year over year (A, C, D).

Citrix's revenue recovered from -9.89% year over year in March to +1.65% in June. Subscription ARR growth of 73.9% supports a September forecast above -5%. By June, deferred maintenance and support revenue had fallen $178.1 million since December, exceeding the $168.9 million subscription increase. I expect the shrinking maintenance balance to pull December-quarter reported revenue down at least 5% year over year (A–C).

Take-Two's June net revenue fell 2.16% year over year, or $18.0 million, while net bookings fell $284.8 million across several franchises. Grand Theft Auto alone supplied 33.7% of revenue. I expect September revenue to remain above -5% year over year and the much larger bookings decline to feed through to a December-quarter revenue decline of at least 5% (A, B, E).

First Solar's June net sales fell 2.06% year over year. Higher third-party module volume partly offset the effect of prior-year project sales and construction, supporting a September forecast above -5%. June sales also benefited from an indemnification settlement. With project revenue uneven and module selling prices under pressure, I forecast a December-quarter sales decline of at least 5% year over year (A, B, D).
